newsitem.title: UK: UK sales pick up in Jan, exceed expectations - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK sales pick up in Jan, exceed expectations - CBI.

text.p: British high street sales picked up in January and exceeded retailers' expectations, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Thursday.

Its latest distributive trades survey found 53 percent of retailers reported higher sales volumes during the month compared with January 1996, while only 17 percent reported lower turnover, giving a positive balance of 36 percent.
This compares with December's positive balance of 33 percent and 31 percent in January 1996.

"Retailers did better in terms of January's sales growth than they had expected as consumers were confident enough to step up their spending," said Alastair Eperon, chairman of the CBI's Distributive Trade Survey panel.
"However, the rate of underlying sales growth eased for the second consecutive month, although the increase in trade remains robust."
Retailers said they expected sales to moderate in February compared with February 1996.
Grocers and confectioners continued to report strong growth while off-licences reported lower volumes than a year ago.
Clothing retailers reported strong growth while footwear and leather shops said there had been a moderate reduction in volumes.

"Sectors closely related to the housing market such as furniture and carpets, durable household goods and hardware reported further sales growth, although only furniture and carpets produced an acceleration in volumes growth," the CBI said.

Motor traders reported sales volume rose slightly in January, although the annual increase was less than expected. "Business was also considered to be just above average for the time of year, though less so than in December," it added.
